log.msg: Measured against a CONTROL run of six shipped layouts, so a finding can be told from a rule that fires everywhere. Control at 1280/3440: document A96/A91 · dashboard A97/B87 · gallery A90/B87 · landing B81/C70 · split B81/C74 · docs D64/C74.

Two verified analyzer gaps, both in rules the parent task is writing right now. (1) `doc-overflow` has no scroller guard — the carousel's rail was confirmed in-browser as scrollWidth 2075 > clientWidth 1280 with scroll-snap live, and every slide waiting off-screen is reported as content past the viewport. false-positives.md already states the principle ('a scroller's content is meant to exceed its box'); doc-overflow does not apply it. (2) `gutter` measured a scroller's clamped text bounds as touching the region edge — fixed on my side by moving the rail's inset to a WRAPPER, since a scroller clips at its own padding box.

Screenshots caught what the analyzer could not: `.measure` hardcodes `margin-inline: auto`, so every capped intro block rendered CENTRED above left-aligned content. There is no left-aligned capped-column utility — the three pages now carry an inline `max-width: 34em`, which is what site.hero() already does. That is the one framework.css request worth having.

Adopting the css-strategy skill's proportion rule — `clamp(1em, 3%, 3.5em)` for band padding instead of a flat 2em — moved hero from A91/B86 to A97/A96 and pricing's 3440 from C71 to B84. Fixed em padding is what `pad-scale` was flagging.
